decisions.decision: Use batch serving for document classification
decisions.context: The insurer processes millions of documents daily, and demand varies seasonally. The brief does not require immediate predictions.
decisions.rationale: Batch serving aligns with high-volume document classification and leaves capacity to scale scheduled processing for seasonal peaks. The checked batch point was novel and unattested; the real-time rival was also novel and unattested (d:5, d:15).
consequences: Consumers read completed predictions from storage.
Classification latency depends on batch schedule.

decisions.context: Incoming volume reaches millions per day and varies over the year. The brief does not specify a real-time response requirement.
decisions.rationale: Batch ingestion matches the batch serving choice and enables processing capacity to be scaled around seasonal demand. The checked batch combination and the real-time rival were both unattested (d:7, d:15).
consequences: Ingestion schedules must accommodate seasonal peaks.
Consumers receive results after processing completes.

decisions.decision: Partition batch processing to scale throughput
decisions.context: The system classifies millions of documents each day, with seasonal changes in volume. Processing needs to scale to the incoming workload.
decisions.rationale: Partitioning provides a way to increase batch throughput as seasonal volume rises. It was selected in the checked batch point; the rival point using no parallel processing was also unattested (d:17).
consequences: Partitions need to be balanced across workers.
Results must be gathered for consumers.

decisions.decision: Monitor model performance and log predictions
decisions.context: Operators need to see when classification quality drifts. Monitoring needs to capture model performance as well as the data and predictions needed to investigate changes.

alternatives.label: Monitoring or logging data and predictions

decisions.rationale: Model performance monitoring directly addresses the brief’s need to see quality drift. Logging data and predictions is a useful complementary practice, but the design-space check permits one value per dimension, so only performance monitoring is selected (d:22).
consequences: Define and track classification performance measures.
Logging details and retention remain to be designed.
